title: Hosted Canary Rollouts (Hosted routes) — GA Change Management Checklist
body:
Owner: Connor O’Brien (Release)
Last reviewed: 2025-04-04
Scope: GA enablement for “Hosted canary rollout workflow” (percentage-based traffic splitting on Hosted routes) including Console UI, control plane schema, policy guardrails, routing enforcement, telemetry + dashboards, audit logging.

This checklist is written for the GA cut + staged enablement (beta → GA) and should be used as the “single source of truth” for release go/no-go readiness and backout steps.

---

1) Release metadata

Release name: Hosted Canary Rollouts — GA
Target window: Week of 2025-04-07 (Mon–Thu)
Primary on-call coverage required: Eng Platform + SRE
Change classification: Customer-facing feature w/ routing dataplane behavior + new policy paths + audit logging
Blast radius: Per-tenant by feature flag; dataplane change affects routing decisions only when rollout config exists OR flag gates are enabled.

Approvers (required for GA flip):
- Product: Marissa Cole (Console & rollouts) + Paula Mendes (policy/telemetry requirements)
- Engineering: Dylan Brooks (Console & tooling), Ethan Park (Control Plane), Mina Haddad (Smart Routing)
- SRE: Sean Gallagher (SRE lead) or Rafael Mendes (on-call manager)
- Security: Marcus Lin (audit logging/RBAC)
- Release: Connor O’Brien

Go/no-go meeting: 30 mins, day-of enablement
Agenda: open Sev bugs, SLO/alert readiness, runbook readiness, kill switch confirmation, audit log verification, staged rollout plan

---

2) Dependencies (must be merged + deployed prior to GA)

Code deployed to production (verify commit SHAs / deploy IDs in deploy tool):
[ ] Smart Routing traffic splitting primitive deployed (GitHub: redwood/pr-28741)
[ ] Rollout Orchestrator API + state machine deployed (GitHub: redwood/pr-28788)
[ ] Policy engine guardrails deployed (GitHub: redwood/pr-28802)
[ ] Telemetry tagging + aggregation hooks deployed (GitHub: redwood/pr-28819)
[ ] Auto-stop / rollback wiring deployed (GitHub: redwood/pr-28845)
[ ] Activity timeline + audit events persistence deployed (GitHub: redwood/pr-28877)
[ ] Cohort dashboards/alert templates available (GitHub: redwood/pr-28910)

RBAC + permissions:
[ ] rollout-approver role + permission mappings deployed (GitHub: rbac-policy-bundle/pr-311)
[ ] Console correctly hides/disables actions when perms missing (create/start/approve/pause/rollback)

Docs readiness:
[ ] Customer docs merged + published (GitHub: redwood-docs/pr-922)
[ ] Internal on-call runbook final (Confluence: runbook-rollout-stuck-or-bad-split)
[ ] Audit event spec final + shared w/ Support/Sales (Confluence: audit-events-rollout-actions)

---

3) Feature flags / config gates

We are using a layered gating approach. GA requires all three layers to be “ready,” but only tenant-level enablement should be expanded.

A) Console UI gating
Flag: console.hosted_canary_rollouts_ui
Default: OFF
Controls: visibility of Rollouts wizard + timeline views in Console
Checklist:
[ ] Flag exists in prod, is writable by release tooling
[ ] Flag OFF behavior is clean (no dead links, no partial panels)
[ ] Flag ON for internal dogfood tenants only pre-GA

B) Control plane / orchestrator gating
Flag: control_plane.hosted_canary_rollouts_orchestrator
Default: ON (recommended) or ON for allowlist only depending on risk call
Controls: create/progress/pause/rollback endpoints acceptance; persistence paths
Checklist:
[ ] Validate no background tasks run for tenants without rollouts configured
[ ] Validate idempotency on action endpoints (retry safe)
[ ] Verify orchestrator emits events even when Console UI is off (API-only tenants)

C) Dataplane enforcement gating
Flag: routing.hosted_route_canary_splitting
Default: ON (recommended) but only used when a rollout is active OR allowlist
Controls: actual traffic splitting enforcement for Hosted routes
Checklist:
[ ] Verify enforcement is no-op unless rollout config present / active
[ ] Verify deterministic cohorting key per ADR (Confluence ADR: cohorting & traffic splitting)
[ ] Verify region behavior matches GA spec (percent is global per route; region-specific metrics available)

Kill switches (must exist + verified):
[ ] Kill switch 1: disable routing enforcement (routing.hosted_route_canary_splitting = OFF)
[ ] Kill switch 2: block new rollouts creation/start for new tenants (control_plane… allowlist mode)
[ ] Kill switch 3: hide Console entry points (console… = OFF)

Kill switch ownership + execution:
Primary: SRE on-call (Sean/Rafael) can flip routing kill switch
Secondary: Release (Connor) can flip Console flag
Tertiary: Control plane on-call (Ethan’s rotation) can switch orchestrator allowlist mode

---

4) Migrations / schema changes

Schema changes (control plane persistence): rollout objects, steps/states, audit/event references (ENG-9131)

Pre-flight:
[ ] Confirm migrations are backward compatible with existing routing policy schema
[ ] Confirm read paths tolerate missing new fields (safe defaults)
[ ] Confirm old Console clients do not crash if new rollout data exists

Execution:
[ ] Migration applied to prod control-plane DB(s) during low-traffic window
[ ] Verify migration completion: no long locks, no replication lag above threshold
[ ] Verify new tables/columns have correct indexes (rollout_id lookups, route_id lookups)

Post-migration validation:
[ ] Create a test rollout in staging and prod-internal tenant; confirm persists and reads back
[ ] Confirm audit event persistence works (rollout_create, rollout_start, step_change, pause, approval, rollback)
[ ] Confirm event retention settings align with security expectations (per audit logging spec)

Rollback stance for migrations:
- Prefer forward-fix: schema additions are not rolled back unless necessary (risk of data loss).
- If hard rollback required: stop all orchestrator writes + disable UI + disable routing enforcement first, then consult DB owner for recovery.

---

5) Monitoring, dashboards, and alerting to watch

Key signals for release window (must be pinned in the “GA watch” dashboard):

A) Routing correctness
[ ] Split adherence: observed canary % vs configured % (global + per-region)
[ ] Cohort assignment stability: % of requests switching cohorts for same user key (should be ~0; watch streaming/retries)
[ ] Retry behavior: ensure retries do not flip cohort unexpectedly

B) Customer-impact SLO signals (baseline vs canary)
[ ] 5xx rate (baseline cohort vs canary cohort)
[ ] timeout rate (baseline vs canary)
[ ] p95 latency (baseline vs canary)
[ ] queue time / admission control signals (if applicable)

C) System health
[ ] Control plane API error rate on rollout endpoints
[ ] Orchestrator background worker lag / stuck transitions
[ ] Metric evaluation timeouts for stop conditions (watch for repeat of beta issue fixed in pr-28895)
[ ] Audit log pipeline: ingestion success rate and export queue depth (if enabled)

Alert policy during GA window (tuning guidance):
- Avoid alert storms: cohort-specific alerts should page only when BOTH: (a) minimum traffic threshold met AND (b) regression above threshold sustained for N minutes.
- Ensure stop-condition triggers do not page twice (auto-pause + alert) unless necessary.

Confirm templates exist:
[ ] Standard cohort comparison panels available (GitHub: observability-pack/pr-184 or redwood/pr-28910)
[ ] Alert templates for auto-stop triggers reviewed by SRE (Sean/Rafael)

---

6) Auto-stop / auto-rollback configuration

Default stop conditions (GA defaults) — confirm they match product decision + SRE sign-off:
[ ] 5xx regression threshold: ____% absolute or ____x relative (fill in final values)
[ ] timeout regression threshold: ____% absolute
[ ] p95 latency regression threshold: +____ ms or +____% over baseline
[ ] Minimum sample size / minimum time window before evaluating: ____
[ ] Soak time minimum between steps: ____ (policy enforced)

Safety checks:
[ ] Confirm auto-stop action is PAUSE by default (vs rollback), unless tenant policy requires rollback
[ ] Confirm rollback is a separate explicit action or only happens after pause + approval (depending on tier)
[ ] Confirm notifications route to correct internal channels for beta/GA (PagerDuty + Slack)

Runbook linkage:
[ ] Stop-condition fired path referenced in runbook (diagnostics, how to resume/rollback)

---

7) Approval gates / policy guardrails verification

Guardrails required for GA (PM-1851):
[ ] Max step size enforced (e.g., cannot jump from 5% to 100% unless policy allows)
[ ] Minimum soak time enforced between step promotions
[ ] Approval required for risky actions (configurable): start rollout, promote above threshold, rollback
[ ] Clear Console error messages on deny with “how to fix” guidance

RBAC behaviors:
[ ] Non-approver cannot approve steps / cannot override guardrails
[ ] Approver role can approve but still cannot exceed hard tenant policy caps
[ ] Audit events record actor, role, IP/user agent (as available), tenant, route, diffs

Edge cases to test (quick checklist):
[ ] Attempt to promote before soak time elapsed → denied, message displayed
[ ] Attempt step > max jump → denied
[ ] Attempt rollback without permission → denied
[ ] Attempt start while missing required metrics (no traffic) → allowed but stop conditions should not thrash

---

8) Release sequencing plan (staged enablement)

Stage 0 — Internal dogfood (already in progress)
[ ] Enable for Redwood internal tenant(s) only
[ ] Run 1–2 real rollouts of non-critical Hosted routes
[ ] Validate audit logs show up in internal audit viewer

Stage 1 — Design partner cohort (beta) stability check
[ ] Confirm no open P0/P1 issues from design partners tracker
[ ] Confirm support escalation path is active (#support-escalations + on-call)

Stage 2 — GA soft launch (allowlist)
Target: 10–20 tenants over first 48 hours
[ ] Enable tenant flag for first batch (coordinate w/ Support + PM)
[ ] Watch dashboards for 1 hour after each batch
[ ] Freeze further enablement if any routing correctness anomalies

Stage 3 — GA broad availability
[ ] Switch default enablement from allowlist → available-by-request → self-serve (per product decision)
[ ] Update support macros and internal enablement how-to

---

9) Backout / incident plan

Principle: Prefer “stop the bleeding” (disable enforcement) over partial rollbacks.

Backout levels (execute in this order for highest safety):

Level 1: Disable routing enforcement (fastest)
- Action: routing.hosted_route_canary_splitting = OFF
- Effect: all traffic goes to baseline routing behavior; rollouts remain visible but do not affect split
- Owner: SRE on-call
- Verification: canary cohort traffic drops to ~0% within 5–10 minutes; error rate normalizes

Level 2: Pause rollouts globally / block new rollouts
- Action: control_plane.hosted_canary_rollouts_orchestrator = allowlist-only OR “writes disabled” mode
- Effect: prevents new rollouts / step promotions; existing rollouts can be paused (manual)
- Owner: Control plane on-call

Level 3: Hide Console UI entry points
- Action: console.hosted_canary_rollouts_ui = OFF
- Effect: customers can’t initiate via Console; reduces load on support while investigation proceeds
- Owner: Release / Console on-call

Level 4: Full service rollback (last resort)
- Roll back orchestrator/routing builds only if a safe previous version is known-good and compatible with new schema.
- Requires: engineering leads approval (Dylan/Ethan/Mina) + SRE approval

Incident triggers (examples):
- Observed split mismatch > 2x expected sustained for > 15 minutes (e.g., config 10%, observed 30%)
- Cross-region inconsistency causing higher-than-expected canary traffic in a single region
- Auto-stop thrashing (pause/resume loops) affecting customer operations
- Audit logging failure for rollout actions (security regression)

Comms plan during incident:
[ ] Start internal incident channel (if Sev2+)
[ ] Notify Support lead (Dev Patel) and create/update customer comms snippet
[ ] For impacted enterprise tenants: direct CSM outreach

---

10) Verification tests (release-day run)

Staging:
[ ] Run E2E: create → start → 1% step → promote → pause → rollback → confirm baseline restored
[ ] Run E2E with approval required: start denied until approver approves
[ ] Force stop-condition breach in staging and verify auto-pause + notification

Production (internal tenant only):
[ ] Create rollout on a low-risk internal Hosted route
[ ] Confirm observed traffic split matches within tolerance (after warmup)
[ ] Confirm dashboards show baseline vs canary metrics with correct tags
[ ] Confirm audit events emitted and visible (and exportable if configured)

Post-enablement spot checks (first external tenants):
[ ] Confirm tenant can see rollout wizard + timeline
[ ] Confirm policy guardrails reflect tenant tier (max step, approvals)
[ ] Confirm support can retrieve rollout_id, state, and recent actions quickly

---

11) Documentation + support readiness

Customer docs:
[ ] “How to run a canary rollout” updated with screenshots and guardrail explanations
[ ] Troubleshooting section includes: split mismatch, auto-paused, stuck step, approval denied

Internal docs:
[ ] How-to enable feature for tenant is accurate and includes sanity checks
[ ] On-call runbook includes: diagnosing wrong split, disabling enforcement, checking cohort tags

Support enablement:
[ ] Support macro for “How do I do a percentage rollout?” includes current GA availability rules
[ ] Escalation template includes required fields: tenant_id, route_id, rollout_id, region, timestamps, expected %

- No multi-armed bandits / dynamic optimization
- Quality gates are optional/manual inputs only; not a blocking automated gate for GA
- Dedicated/Private parity not in GA scope; ensure schema compatibility only
